ai_show_review.summary: Epic Lovelight jam with soaring Jerry guitar and Pigpen organ
ai_show_review.blurb: The set moves from a solid first half into an explosive second set anchored by a 21‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry Garcia prowls the stage like a panther, delivering scorching leads while Pigpen’s organ shines on Sitting On Top Of The World. Tuning issues bite in Morning Dew but the band stays locked in.
ai_show_review.review: June 13, 1969 at the Fresno Convention Center captures the Dead in a transitional phase where the psychedelic edge meets the emerging jam‑heavy ethos. After a concise opener with Hard To Handle and Me And My Uncle, the group rolls into Pigpen’s soulful organ on Sitting On Top Of The World before launching into tight renditions of Good Morning Little School Girl* and China Cat Sunflower. The first set stays mostly restrained, but the momentum builds dramatically when Saint Stephen segues straight into The Eleven – a wild, time‑signature stretch that showcases Phil Lesh’s ripping bass lines and the dual drumming of Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann keeping the groove alive despite loose machine heads. The climax arrives with an unforgettable 21‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight; Tom Constanten’s keyboards are crystal clear, Jerry tears it up with panther‑like leads, and the rhythm section drives the jam to a euphoric peak. A brief dip in Morning Dew’s tuning can’t dampen the overall excitement, making this show a standout early‑’70s snapshot of the Dead’s evolving improvisational fire.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard capture with crisp mix, full band balance and the epic Lovelight jam intact.
